Subject: Quick recap & sizing worksheet (follow-up from today's call)

Alex — thanks again for the time this morning. Below is a short recap from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Summary of customer goals / constraints
- Workload: real-time clinical inference for document classification + PHI redaction.
- Peak concurrency target: ~120 concurrent requests (expected burst to 250 for 5–10 minutes).
- Latency target: p99 generation latency <= 350ms for short prompts (~128 tokens).
- Isolation requirement: HITRUST / PHI handling — tenant isolation + private VPC required.
- Data residency: US-only region, strict egress controls.

Key pain points you called out
- Current on-prem setup can't scale past 40 concurrent sessions without dropping below latency SLOs.
- Procurement requires clear activation & termination dates, and monthly commit visibility.
- Need an ops runbook for failover (secondary region) and graceful degradation for critical workflows.

What Redwood recommends (initial sizing & approach)
- Dedicated pool recommendation: 8x A40-equivalent GPUs (reserved) with burst pool of 2x on-demand for traffic surges.
- Isolation: Private deployment model (VPC) with per-tenant encryption keys (KMS) and network ACLs.
- Performance knobs: CPU-backed pre-warm for KV cache + 4-token batching to keep p99 low during bursts.
- SLA target we can commit to for Dedicated: 99.9% availability (proposal pending commercial review).

Attachments sent with this note: delta_capacity_workbook.xlsx (worksheets: utilization, burst-scenarios), network_requirements.pdf (VPC checklist).

Immediate next steps
1) You to confirm the typical request size distribution and any off-hours batch windows (Alex).
2) Naomi to share the filled capacity worksheet and a rough TCO estimate by EOD Thursday (me).
3) Aditya will follow up with a short ops runbook draft and pre-warm checklist (Aditya, by next Tue).
4) Procurement to share procurement timeline and preferred contract term (Procurement).

Please reply inline if anything above is off — otherwise we'll treat these as the agreed items and proceed to a pricing/term sketch.

Best,
